Both pedestrians suffered injuries as a result of the collision
Alcohol was determined to be a factor by the police who responded to the accident
rationale_highlights: the respondent grew up in a home where alcohol use and abuse was a regular occurrence
there are a number of relevant factors that would warrant a shorter custodial sentence than sought by the Crown, including the Gladue factors

crime_highlights: an out-of-control van came up over the curb and struck his vehicle
Tragically, Mr. Blackburn died of his injuries a few hours later
The out-of-control vehicle was driven by the appellant, Cecil Anthony Boutilier, who had stolen it from a nearby dealership just minutes before
Mr. Boutilier fled the scene on foot
rationale_highlights: very difficult life as an African Nova Scotian - Mi’kmaq man was also properly considered
After considering all the relevant factors, the judge settled on a 7.5 year prison sentence
note: Appeal only on remand credit; court never states effect of Gladue or IRCA factors.
